explanation: There's no basis for treating the head as 'the seat of the soul' in Islamic teaching — a well-known hadith actually encourages gently stroking an orphan's head as an act of kindness, so the gesture toward children reads as affectionate rather than offensive. Toward an adult, patting the head is more about overfamiliarity and perceived disrespect for someone's dignity or status than any religious violation.
local_tip: Keep head-patting to children you know, and greet adults with a handshake (same gender) or a verbal greeting instead.

also_check.note: The head is considered the most sacred part of the body, so touching it, child or adult, is a serious breach of etiquette.
Patting a child's head is often affectionate, but touching an adult's head is seen as disrespectful, especially by a stranger.
Patting an adult's head generally reads as condescending outside of close friendships.

sources.title: Hadith on Orphans: Be kind to orphans for a soft heart
